title: Grateful Dead Live at Temple University on 1970-05-16

ai_review.summary: A decent 1970 audience tape with strong instrument presence but low vocals and occasional cut‑outs; the band delivers a solid, professional college‑gig performance.
ai_review.review: The recording captures the band close to the stage, giving the guitars and other instruments good punch while the vocal mix suffers and some sections are lost to Sam Cutler’s interference. Musically the show is respectable for a 1970 college date – the Dead “dig deep” and stay professional even if the set isn’t legendary. Overall it’s worth a listen for devoted fans who can overlook the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers note decent musical performance (average‑to‑good) but consistent recording problems (instrument focus, low vocals, cuts). Weighted average of show and tape quality yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Close‑to‑stage mic gives strong instrument presence; vocal levels are low and PA is under‑represented. Several sections appear cut or missing, likely due to Sam Cutler’s interference.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical 1970 college gig set; the band stays professional and “dig deep,” though no specific highlights are mentioned by reviewers.
